per_report.trust: High for the literature (TIMELI, VIABench, EgoVoice, WorldScribe, ForeSightGuide, Agarwal et al., Raman et al., ASSETS 2025 ChatGPT study all confirmed to exist with the stated authors, dates and venues). Medium for conclusions, because the report repeats the 0.525 vs 0.20 'cost of one-sided feedback' as its main publishable result, and the algo report's reproduced runs undercut that.

flags.claim: What is strong and publishable is the measured cost of one-sided feedback: 0.525 full information vs about 0.20 one-sided, about 60% of learnable recall (Bottom line 5; Not done item 2; section 3b).
flags.evidence: In seeforme/online/policy.py:143-144, decide() calls _learn_full_info at every 0.5 s step with zero delay. The algo agent's logs in scratchpad/alg/ (full_info+dv.log, fi_s1.log, fi_s2.log) show full information delayed to video end at 0.200/0.206/0.194, with 2 s delay at 0.369 and 12 s delay at 0.206. The 0.525 therefore measures zero-delay labels, not the one-sided channel.
flags.fix: Drop '60% of learnable recall' and 'first measurement of the cost of one-sided feedback' as claims. If any gap claim is kept, it must compare against a causal (delayed) full-information reference, and the delay must be stated.

flags.claim: EgoBlind: 1,392 videos (1,329 clips of about 40 s).
flags.evidence: arXiv 2503.08221v4 HTML reports 1,329 clips cut from 478 long-form videos. The figure 1,392 does not appear there.
flags.fix: Write '1,329 clips from 478 source videos (https://arxiv.org/html/2503.08221v4)'.

flags.claim: Only 541 of 5,311 questions were asked in situ; the rest are GPT-4o generated or written afterwards by blind annotators.
flags.evidence: The paper says 541 questions were manually extracted from the video and about 300 were added by blind volunteers, out of roughly 16,560 GPT-4o candidates. It does not say how many of the 541 survived final filtering.
flags.fix: Say 'at most about 541 of the 5,311 final questions come from the wearer in situ (pre-filter count, arXiv 2503.08221v4)'. Check whether the annotation file marks question source before building the in-situ slice.

per_report.trust: High. The code path is confirmed (_learn_full_info is called inside decide at every step, policy.py:143-144). Its logs exist and match the reported numbers (dv 0.200/0.206/0.194; d2 0.369; d12 0.206; lr0 0.138). The stale summary_dev.md is confirmed: its apple row reads 0.281 at 3.96 cues/min, against 0.169 in online.md. Its citations check out (Raman et al. COLT 2024 with the Θ(1)/Θ(√T)/Θ(T) trichotomy). The weak spot is wording: calling the effect 'leakage'.

flags.claim: The 0.53 upper bound comes from label leakage.
flags.evidence: The decision at time t uses scores computed before the update, so there is no leak within a step. The label at t is available at t+0.5 s, which is standard full-information online learning with zero delay. The real issue is that the comparison mixes feedback type with delay: question labels arrive up to about 10.5 s late. The 'dv' learner also still receives all one-sided feedback.
flags.fix: Call it 'a zero-delay full-information reference, not a causal one'. State that the delayed variants also include the one-sided signals.

flags.claim: In the simulator every question is asked, so on the scored region the problem is delayed full information.
flags.evidence: docs/online.md says 'Questions are always asked'. feedback.py has no p_ask parameter.
flags.fix: None. p_ask is a valid next experiment.

messages_to_agents: PAPER WRITER: Do not claim 'one-sided feedback costs about 60% of learnable recall' or cite 0.525 as an upper bound. The full-information learner gets labels with zero delay (seeforme/online/policy.py:143). With labels delayed to video end it scores 0.200/0.206/0.194, which ties greedy at 0.204. Any gap claim needs a causal reference with a stated delay.

PAPER WRITER: Replace 'Be My Eyes, Seeing AI, Lookout answer only when asked' with 'deployed apps wait to be asked or speak by fixed, content-gated rules (Seeing AI Short Text; Lookout Explore, beta: https://support.google.com/accessibility/android/answer/9031274); none learns when to speak'. Cite Project Astra ('can intuitively start conversations', https://deepmind.google/models/project-astra/) and Guided Vision (launched 2026-10-01, not for navigation, https://www.androidauthority.com/gemini-live-guided-vision-launch-3718122/) as nearest systems.

PAPER WRITER: Treat 'when to speak' and 'one-sided online learning' as prior art: TIMELI (ICRA 2026, arXiv 2609.05596), VIABench (arXiv 2607.14660), WorldScribe (UIST 2024), EgoVoice (EMNLP 2026, arXiv 2610.12248), Agarwal-Gentile-Marinov (arXiv 2302.03784, no venue listed), and Raman et al. (COLT 2024, arXiv 2310.19064). Present the contribution as a new problem instance with an empirical characterisation, not a new setting.

PAPER WRITER: EgoBlind has 1,329 clips from 478 videos, not 1,392. In-situ wearer questions number at most 541 (pre-filter). State that most question timestamps and 'miss' labels are simulated. Taps are simulated with p_tap 0.5, and questions are always asked (p_ask=1).

PAPER WRITER: Select has 11 coverable events per seed. Ratios like 9/33 are pooled over 3 seeds on 11 distinct events. Do not present select-based choices as statistically supported. OKO is free since July 2025; do not use it as a subscription-backlash example without that date.
